Cost grid evaluated for all 10 tickers x 3 lookbacks x 3 cost levels via stress_segments with a matched coin-flip null at the same cfg; artifact written to state/check_artifacts/momentum_cost_sensitivity_results.json.

Primary result: net-of-cost candidate medians are essentially INVARIANT to the cost level -- universe cross-asset median of lookback-5 candidate medians = 0.069 at zero, realistic, AND conservative. Costs do not erase the momentum signal's positive return pattern.

Predeclared verdict-based classification: COST_ROBUST=5 (AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA), COST_ERODED=1 (MSFT), NO_EDGE=4 (NVDA, JPM, JNJ, XOM). Median-based cross-check (robust to the null-dispersion label): COST_ROBUST=9, NO_EDGE=1 (NVDA).

The 4-asset gap between the two rules (MSFT, JPM, JNJ, XOM) is a null-dispersion verdict artifact, NOT a cost effect: their lookback-5 candidate medians are unchanged and positive across all cost levels; only the matched null's dispersion changes, flipping the REGIME_STABLE/CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE label. Documented in the artifact as caveats.

Mechanism confirmed by turnover diagnostic: the persistent momentum sign rarely flips, so full-sample turnover is low (~14-31x over ~17 years, <2x/yr) for most assets and the conservative cost drag is only 0.02-0.09 of cumulative return; NVDA is the exception (turnover 81x, drag 0.707, its negative segment deepens -0.038 -> -0.088).
A-priori prediction (majority COST_ERODED/NO_EDGE due to high turnover) is FALSIFIED: the edge is cost-robust because turnover is low, not high.

Independent verifier: Gate 1 fresh walk_forward + noise_benchmark recomputation MATCH for AMZN/JPM at every cost level x lookback (candidate medians AND matched null); Gate 2 zero-cost column cross-consistency vs momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json MATCH (all 10 tickers x 3 lookbacks); Gate 3 both cost-robustness classes reproduce from artifact medians/verdicts; determinism r1==r2 identical.
